title: Alignment to an external scheme with no code
statement: A denominator larger than the numerator means the fraction has to be written the other way round, because the smaller number always belongs on top.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: write the fraction shown by a diagram where the shaded count exceeds one whole
evidence_patterns.signature: numerator and denominator are swapped whenever the numerator would be the larger of the two

example.item: Write the fraction for 7 shaded thirds.

discriminators.vs_slip: Consistent: the learner swaps every improper fraction, and says the larger number belongs underneath when asked.

alignments.note: Deliberately missing `code`. This fixture exists to prove the schema rejects an external-scheme alignment with no code; it must fail for that reason and no other.

sources.citation: Ashlock, R. B. (2010). Error Patterns in Computation: Using Error Patterns to Help Each Student Learn (10th ed.). Allyn & Bacon.

provenance.notes: Test fixture only. Not a claim about the corpus.

changelog.change: Created as the fixture for the alignment-code requirement.
